title: Navigation in React Native
description: Learn how to navigate between screens using React Navigation, including stack, tab, and drawer navigators.

lessons.title: What is Navigation and Why It’s Important
lessons.content: In mobile apps, navigation refers to moving between different screens or views. React Native apps often use libraries like React Navigation to handle transitions and screen hierarchies easily.

lessons.title: Installing React Navigation
lessons.content:
To get started, install the required packages:

```bash
npm install @react-navigation/native
npx expo install react-native-screens react-native-safe-area-context
npm install @react-navigation/native-stack
```

If you're using bare React Native:

```bash
npm install react-native-screens react-native-safe-area-context react-native-gesture-handler react-native-reanimated react-native-vector-icons
```
And don't forget to wrap your app in `NavigationContainer`.

Nesting Navigators (Stack in Tab, etc.)
lessons.content: You can nest navigators to build complex UI flows. For example, use a Tab Navigator inside a Stack Navigator to allow switching between tabs on one screen and pushing new screens on another.

lessons.title: Best Practices in Navigation
lessons.content:
- Use unique screen names
- Pass minimal data through navigation (use global state when needed)
- Handle back actions on Android properly
- Avoid nesting more than two levels unless necessary
